**Joshua 19:47**
*And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.*

**Judges 17-18** tells the story of Micah, his creation of his own church full of idols and icons, an ephod and teraphim, and his recruiting of a young Levite to be his personal house priest, calling him "father."

In those days there was no king in Israel. And men did as seemed right in their own eyes.

The story presented occurs during the period immediately after Joshua's death, where Dan had not fully gone out to take their inheritance from those that dwelled there.

**Joshua 23:4-5**
*Behold, I have divided unto you by lot these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even unto the great sea westward. And the LORD your God, he shall expel them from before you, and drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess their land, as the LORD your God hath promised unto you.*

Joshua had waxed old and died before the tribes had finished the work to go out and possess the land given them. Dan especially was shown to be dragging behind the other tribes.

And here they are seeking to go out and find land to take. In **Judges 18**, we find that the troop of spies stop at Mt Ephraim, and lodge at the house of Micah. There they recognized the young Levite, and inquire why he's there. He tells them of the arrangements made with Micah, his hire and role as a private priest over a house of gods.

They ask him for God's blessings in finding a suitable city to take, and he says reassuring words that God had blessed their endeavors. And so, 600 Danites set forth to go into the land, armed for war.

They come up on the house of Micah and the spies tell their army about the gods and the silver graven image and the ephod and priest, and they go in and take all the idols and ephod for themselves. The priest protests and they tell him to come with them and be their priest, and he agrees.

Micah seeing this runs out with some men from his town and Micah confronts them. The much larger force of men gathered for war tell him to stop, or he may forfeit his and his family's lives.

And so Dan finds the city of Laish, or Leshem, and the people there living simple and peaceful lives, and take it for themselves, renaming the city Dan.

And the young priest of the Levites turns out to be the son of Gershom, he and his sons, with their stolen idols and icons and fake Ephod, become the priests for the tribe of Dan until the captivity of the land. The seeds of their own downfall sown by rejecting the way of the Lord and turning to idols.

A people can seem mighty, and put many simple peasants to the sword while carrying the banner of conquest, and relying on idols and images. Unqualified priests. But in the end, God will judge them and their abominations.

Danites went marching on a crusade with their apostate priest and easily took the land, but lost their understanding. The parallel with Roman Catholics should be obvious. The end of those people being captivity and destruction, if they don't turn from Idolatry, repenting towards the Lord.

**Joshua 13** maps for us visual types.

With the majority of the warfare over. And the Lord having delivered the Israelites the land, and Joshua, who was with Moses from the beginning of the exodus, is getting old, God commands the land be apportioned, beginning east of the Jordan in the area Moses had promised Gad, Manasseh and Ruben. And of the Levites, a place in each so their priestly inheritance may be practiced in the sacrifices they maintained.

We see potential for trouble in that there are still strangers of the Canaanites among them. The seeds planted that will cause problems down the line.

As the book of **Numbers** begins to wind down, and Moses nears the end of his life, the Lord reiterates His ordinances and feasts. There is a new high priest. The men of the first generation having all died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua.

The Lord lays out the requirements for the continual burnt sacrifices and sabbath sacrifices and the offerings made for sin.

Each has its specific requirements, varying by the day or type. The offerings of lambs or kids or bullocks. The flour and oil to be given. And the drink offerings poured out.

All a picture of Jesus. All a continuous savor to the Lord. As the children of Israel reach the promised land, they are called to remember these ordinances for all time, that their faith in the Lord not be forgotten, and His favor given them.

Verse 7 contains a description of the drink offering.

*And the drink offering thereof shall be the fourth part of an hin for the one lamb: in the holy place shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured unto the Lord for a drink offering.*

This is a verse that could be used to defend the consumption of alcohol, or the blasphemy of using fermented wine at the Lord's supper, although it rarely is.

But the prohibition against the priests consumption of strong wine;

**Leviticus 10:8-9**
*And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying, Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations:*

...and the numerous places in scripture that teach against it present a problem for those seeking to use this verse to justify it.

But what then? First, we see the drink offering is to be poured out with the burnt offering, which is a continual fire. Alcoholic strong drink would feed the fire, where new wine would quench it. Also, where fermented juices store easily, there is the idea that in the wilderness it would be easiest to obtain and have on hand for the purpose of a twice daily sacrifice.

Ellicott's Commentary states:
(7) Shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured . . . --Better, pour out the drink offering of strong drink. The word shecar, which is here rendered "strong wine," denotes any kind of intoxicating drink, whether made from grapes, honey, or grain; but it is more frequently used to denote a drink which is not made from grapes, as, e.g., in Leviticus 10:9, where the command is given to Aaron and his sons not to drink "wine nor strong drink" (shecar) when they went into the tent of meeting. In the parallel passage in Exodus, the drink offering was to consist of "the fourth part of an hin of wine" (Numbers 29:40). (Comp. Numbers 15:5.) In Exodus 30:9 it is forbidden to pour any drink offering upon the altar of incense, from which passage it has been inferred that the drink offerings were poured upon the altar of burnt sacrifice.

The indication that strong wine is liquor from other sources than grapes, which has weak fermentation.

Matthew Henry commentary says;
The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17.

I only note these to show that this passage is unique in what it commands, and the reason unclear other than to suppose it is a libation for God, and His will it be offered.

**Revelation 1:18-20**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

This week, we are going to look at the messages to the churches in Asia Minor that are addressed by Jesus in His revelation to John. I want to focus on a very specific aspect to these churches; even the worst had members who were right with God. 

There are some strange doctrines around these, the most common of which is that the churches represent some "church age," and that they describe a period of time, rather than the types of behaviors described. Others make these verses to be about individual people, and personal salvation when, as we see in the above passages, Christ is talking about groups of people and the candle is the assembly, not individuals. 

But these are literal places and people, real actual churches, and the lessons given are to serve as a model for our churches today. And a lesson for those who think they are too righteous for church, and so they forsake the assembly.

**Revelation 2:1-6**
*Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks; I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted. Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate*.

The Ephesians, a well known church in the NT, has been around at this point for about 40 years. We know it was established during Paul's evangelizing around AD 60, and John is writing in mid-90 AD. They are given a mostly positive review by Christ. 

They are right on doctrine. They are right on preaching against false doctrines Christ hates. They rejected false Apostles, labor for God and are faithful, yet they have been lacking in their first love. Most see this as meaning soul-winning. Evangelizing to others, as we are called to do. 

While we as individuals can certainly serve as a witness to Christ and give the gospel to the lost, winning them to Jesus, the assembly of believers is called to do this in an organized way, and to provide a place for discipleship once someone is saved. A place for baptism and service. Edifying, that is building-up, the congregation. Training others to go out into the world, preaching to every creature. 

As good as Ephesians are, their lack of this is sufficient for Christ to rebuke them. 

But what does this mean for us today? 

It means that we need to encourage the brethren to do all those positive things mentioned that the church at Ephesus does, while not forgetting that first love. 

Does this mean if the local NT Christian churches in our area don't have an organized soul-winning campaign, we shouldn't attend? Does Christ command that? Does He say it is a prerequisite that it must have before you join them? No. 

If the church's candlestick is snuffed out, it will be by the Lord deciding. In the meantime there's plenty to do that is positive, and perhaps your contributions are to help them repent towards that first love again. 

Go to church!

I will cover a church a day, but I will take this time to establish some definitions and doctrines.

Church is a called out assembly of believers. The people of God are required to come when called together. This was true in the OT and it is true in the New. 

We see the consequences in **Judges 21** of those who forsake the assembly. Jabeshgilead was wiped out:

*Go and smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the children. And this is the thing that ye shall do, Ye shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman that hath lain by man.*

There are consequences for not assembling when called. 

"A church is not a place it's a people!" So true, but the people need a place to gather, and having one fixed location and time makes that possible. Preferably a place with a roof and protection from the elements. Maybe with chairs, since you'll be there a while. Lights and heat and AC would be great. Hey, why not a building dedicated to that purpose?

You see the sophistry of saying it's not a place, when you actually stop and consider what that means. 

Well what about when Jesus says *"For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them"* Yes! Wonderful promise of the Lord, that He blesses us with His presence when we gather together in His name! 

This presupposes you are actually gathering. It's not an excuse to not.

"But it's getting bad out there, Satan is everywhere! So many false churches with bad doctrine!"

All the more reason to get plugged into a local church:

**Hebrews 10:24-25**
*And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching. 
*
This appeal is explicitly about what we should do because things are getting worse, not an excuse not to. 

**Colossians 3:16**
*Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.*

Can't do that from your sofa.

**Revelation 2:8-11 **
*And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive; I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.*

To the church as Smyrna, a real place with real people, Jesus gave a message. He knows their works and their tribulation. He knows they have been persecuted by the Jews. He knows what members of a church may suffer, and encourages them to have no fear, even unto death, because they have the crown of life in Him. 

It is easy to see the hope and encouragement in the face of persecution for the faith. In fact, God tells us if we choose to live for Him, it is inevitable:

**2 Timothy 3:12**
*Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.*

But what does it mean to live godly in Christ? Well, for one it means to be in church. The saints at Smyrna were gathered together, and doing works that despite their poverty made them rich in the eyes of the Lord. And that brought persecution of the Jews against them. 

You will not be persecuted for the faith if you are practicing it in private, online, as a shut in. You are not doing works God sees and knows. You are not drawing attention of the enemies of Christ. You certainly aren't going to earn rewards in heaven for persecution that never happened. You won't be put in jail for Christ, not even 1 day. 

Being banned from social media or a chatroom isn't persecution. 

It takes being an open member of a congregation doing works for the Lord to stand out and be set upon by Satan. 

**Romans 5:1-5**
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

Go to church!

**1 Timothy 3:14-15**
*These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly: But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.*

Paul, writing to Timothy one of the Pastoral Epistles, is literally the section of the NT dealing with the hierarchy and qualifications of the churches being planted then, and standards we hold today. God establishes the offices of Bishop, or overseer, or as we say in English, a pastor. As well as deacons, to aid in the running of the affairs of the church. And what is the local church described as by the Apostle in the Spirit?

According to Paul the local church is the house of God, and a pillar and ground of truth. 

**Genesis 28:10-22**
*And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran. And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the Lord stood above it, and said, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven. And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.*

Jacob rested on the rock, the word of God. And there he set the rock as a pillar of truth, anointed as holy, separate. And he established that this pillar is of the house of God, and pledged his tithe, the tenth of all God gives him towards that cause. 

Notice it is "the tenth," not "a tenth." This was an established idea. Tithing was understood even before this. 

All this to say, the church is a house of God and pillar and ground of truth, built on the rock that is His word. And to it we should give the tenth of all God has given us. Tithe. 

Your computer chair is not the pillar and ground of truth. You are not giving God the tenth from your couch. You must be in a called out assembly of believers to do these things. 

Go to church. And tithe.

**Revelation 2:12-16 **
*And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges; I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes, which thing I hate. Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth*.

The church at Pergamos was located in a city of committed idolatry. Pergamon was a wealthy city of trade and a center for the worship of Greek gods like Zeus and Dionysus. It was also known for its healing sanctuary dedicated to the god Asclepius. 

Satan's seat, according to Jesus. 

And because of the dedication to false gods and Idolatry, the believers in the church there suffered persecution, including the martyrdom of one of their own, Antipas.

There are no martyrs for the faith without outward, visible signs of preaching and service. No one is going door to door to ask. No one is tracing your Telegram posts to see what you've read or liked. 

Despite this church having perseverance in the face of persecution, they had allowed others to creep in who taught the evil of Idolatry. Eating that which was given to idols. As well as fornication, and the licentious heresy of the Nicolaitanes who taught that the liberty of Christ and the grace that abounds from God means you can and should sin. Jesus repeats that He hates this false doctrine. 

"The churches near me are full of hypocrites! They have some tertiary doctrines I don't agree with!" Are they offering meat unto idols? Ritual fornication and the license to sin? 

Jesus said to remove the blatantly false doctrines from among them, and cast out the weirdos and damnable heretics. He didn't tell them to stop going to church. 

If your nearby churches are wrong about the timing of the rapture, so what? They don't hold your view on the shape of the realm? Who cares? 

If they still teach the right gospel, and are Biblically sound on primary doctrine, you will be able to say "See, I told you so!" as you high-five each other in the clouds as you're gathered to Christ. (Or humbly admit "I was wrong.")

The assembly of believers in Pergamon had it far worse, and dealt with evil heretics and persecution, and still they assembled together. Still a candlestick was lit for that church. Still Jesus gave them encouragement and praise with His criticism. 

Go to church, even if you have minor disagreement with others there.
I will note that Jesus did not have John write letters to individual Christians. His word for was assemblies of believers, gathered as a congregation in independent local churches.

**Deuteronomy 24:19-20**
*When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands. When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.*

As a reminder that God has provided a system to feed the poor, called gleaning, where the owner of a vineyard or orchard does not go back over the field after harvest to get every last morsel of fruit left in the vine, but instead leaves it for the poor to gather. 

This is in addition to the expectation of a tithe. 

Personal charity and alms are an expectation for Christians. Being a cheerful giver is something God loves. Along with hospitality and sharing our things with those in need, especially among the brethren. 

There are spiritual applications to gleaning, sharing that which we have learned with one another at church. But also the literal. We all have more than we need or deserve, blessed by God. We don't need to horde all of it. We can take the excess to the assembly, and offer it to those who could use it. In addition to tithing. 

I bring extra tomatoes and peppers from my garden. Some bring eggs. Some bring talents and trades and skills. Hand-me-downs and excess clothing. 

Church can be a center for this type of charity. For gleaning. To help those among you or for the fatherless and the windows. 

You can certainly give to people outside of church, and should. But being part of a church community creates infrastructure and connections you may not get anywhere else.

Certainly not in a Discord server posing as a church. Or in a chat room.

**Revelation 2:18-25 **
*And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write; These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet are like fine brass; I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first. Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols. And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works. But unto you I say, and unto the rest in Thyatira, as many as have not this doctrine, and which have not known the depths of Satan, as they speak; I will put upon you none other burden. But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.*

Here, Jesus speaks directly to members of a church divided by false doctrines, where not only have they allowed fornication and eating food sacrificed to idols to creep in, but it appears ritual fornication with a woman suffered to teach, proclaiming herself to be a prophetess. Seducing the men, and apparently having many bastards children. 

Thyatira was located just 35 miles southeast of Pergamum, and was equally wealthy. The woman Lydia, the seller of purple cloth who was won to Christ by Paul, was from this city (**Acts. 16:14-15**). It was filled with Idolatry to Zeus and the Roman gods, and progressive morally, where a woman could become a wealthy business woman, or mislead a congregation into sin.

Even so, Jesus speaks these words to those in the congregation that have maintained the faith; *I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first.*

Their works for God are so great, He named them twice, that they are growing exponentially the last more than the first. Their faith, charity and service are enough to be seen of Christ and acknowledged by Him. Despite that Jezebel they've allowed in. 

In the midst of one of the most wicked churches described here, there are those doing well, great works for the Lord. 

For the wicked, He will repay. They shall be made to know He is the Lord. Her children will die, she will be bedridden with venereal disease, and all those who laid with her. And all the churches, plural, will know He is the Lord.

Jesus encouraged the people in Thyatira who didn't know about this evil, or didn't participate in it, to hold fast. To continue in the faith until He comes. 

I don't care what you think goes on in your local churches, it isn't the depths of Satan found in Thyatira. 

Jesus says throughout these letters to the various churches that He has seen the works they've done in service for God. Together. As a group. As a called out assembly of believers. 

*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

And everywhere, Jesus talks about churches, plural. Local, independent congregations. There is no other hierarchy given, but Christ as the head, and pastor overseeing the flock in their assembly. 

*To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ...As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ; Who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit....And He is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.*

*Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;) And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia: Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ*...

*Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.*

These were real places, with real people, attending real churches. They heard the word of God by letter, proclaimed in the Spirit for their edification and for ours. 

You are not receiving the fullness of the word or ability to act on it in service to God without those assemblies found in nearly every town and city.

Go to church

**Revelation 3:1-6**
*And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee. Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. 
*
One of the most common push-backs against going to church is that churches are "dead." That all the congregations in the area are filled with elderly women, senior saints, and a pastor managing the decline, whose ministry is deathbeds and funerals. 

It is not an indictment of churches, but younger generations not replenishing the pews. 

Sardis, which apparently had a reputation thought the region of being a great church doing great things for the Lord, is becoming dead. Jesus warns them to strengthen that which they have left, before He snuffs out the candlestick of their assembly. 

Young blood revitalizes an old church. 

Even in Sardis, there were believers who kept the faith and remembered that word which they had heard. Who are saved. Even if the rest were lifeless, and dead. Just going to go and not believing unto salvation. 

What a blessing it would be for those hanging on for that glorious day, and who would strengthen the works that remained, by having young red hot Christians to help them. What great things young people could do for the Lord by being a blessing to them. 

And for a pastor to be reinvigorated by the new sheep added to the flock. To look out at what was a dying church and see new life again. To plan baptisms and weddings instead of funerals.

Go to church. Even if you are 40yrs younger than the youngest member. Even if it is uncomfortable at first. Learn from them. Help. Be used by God. 

Go to church.

**Romans 10:8-9**
*But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.*

Born-again Christians are familiar with this beautiful verse, proclaiming the gospel by which we stand. What follows is equally important, and applies to those of us who have already called upon the name of the Lord.

**Romans 10:13-15**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!*

How shall they hear without a preacher, how shall they preach without being sent. This is the first love of a church, and the great commission we have been given by Jesus as Christians. To be sent into the world, preaching the good news to every creature. 

To be sent requires a sender. To be skilled in preaching requires a tutor. An instructor in the faith. We are given the model of soul-winning by how Christ Himself sent out the apostles. 

**Luke 10:1-3**
*After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come. And traveling out to compel people to come to the Lord wasn't a new concept in the New Testament. Above, Paul was quoting Isaiah:

**Isaiah 52:7**
*How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!*

As it is said; **Proverbs 11:30**
*The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.*

If you are not in a church, who is sending you out, two by two? Who is organizing it? 

Go to church.

**Revelation 3:7-11**
*And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth; I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. The church at Philadelphia gets off the easiest from Christ's letters to the various independent churches of Asia Minor. They have kept the faith with patience and done great works, deserving crowns. They have everlasting life and the promise of Jesus that the Jews who persecuted them will be made to know He loves them. This promise extends to all who have overcome in Christ Jesus. 

Believe it or not, despite what charlatans online say, there are churches like this today. You can likely find a church full of salt of the earth believers in every county in the US, or within driving distance of one. 

Churches with the right gospel, the right mindset, filled with people who love the Lord with patience and faith, doing great works for the Lord, building each other up in persecution and edifying themselves in the word. 

And the crowns they earn for themselves in the Kingdom do not rust or mold. They last forever. But that is not something available to you at home, alone, consuming Rumble videos and listening to weirdos spout nonsense. 

True discipleship comes from joining the local church to be a worker for the Lord.

**Revelation 3:14-19**
*And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God; I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.

As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.*

The church at Laodicea is probably the most talked about in these seven letters to the seven churches. Many have some mistaken idea that the 7 churches represent 7 "church ages," and that we are in the "Laodicean age." That churches are generally lukewarm now, and it's just how it is. This is foolish. 

But this foolish idea has led many to abandon church altogether. 

"If Jesus is disgusted by their lukewarm Christianity, then I don't want to even bother!"

Of course there are churches who are like all of these seven, and the model of each is given by Christ to John as a warning to us not to veer towards the negative things that any of them do. 

When faced with a lukewarm church, not facing much persecution, comfortable in their lot in life, just doing the bare minimum, lukewarm, the answer isn't to become cold to church and drop out, it is to become red hot for the Lord and heat things up. 

Be zealous! Add fire to your local assembly. Zeal is contagious. Humbly seek to serve God in the called out assembly, and watch it get red hot for the Lord.

Go to church!

Wrapping up this pre-Christmas series encouraging saved believers to join their local called out assembly, I want to add one last benefit to regular church attendance and membership in the local body; Every saved believer has a difficult time preaching to their loved ones, and getting friends and relatives saved. 

**Matthew 13:54-58**
*And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works? Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? And his sisters, are they not all with us? *But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.*

Wrapping up **Proverbs 25**, we come to a verse which changed my own understanding of dealing with my enemies and improved my Christian walk, and my quality of life. 

*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.*

Verse 21-22 is repeated by Paul, with more encouragement; 

**Romans 12:17-21** 
*Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord. Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.*

These truths seem paradoxical to the mind of man. If someone offends you, harms you or appears to harm you and yours, the natural man reaction is to respond in kind. To render evil for evil. To take vengeance. But God's way says to pray for your enemy. 

**Matthew 5:38-39**, **44-45**
*Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also...But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

This better way of righteousness, where your kindness and meekness in the face of persecution and revilement by others, places the onus entirely on them. 

Rather than rising to their railings, and giving them justification for their wicked behavior, it heals hot coals on their heads. Or maybe, your soft answer will turn away wrath. Your meekness may put them to shame, and they repent. Perhaps your chaste conversation will win them to Christ and make them brothers. Whatever the case, you've been pleasing to God and He will repay. 

**1 Peter 3:8-17**
*Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing. For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it. For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil. And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.*

Bless them that curse you. It will change your life and make it so much more fulfilling and blessed.

The chapter finishes with a series of sayings that echo or reinforce previously made points. God's word tends to do that to drive the point home. Man's minds need repetition. But these sayings add depth to the wisdom, and are as valuable as gold. 

Having an angry countenance, wearing your wrath on your face and complaining about those who've "wronged you" behind their back, to others, drives away people. It's a nasty habit that makes you unpleasant to be around. Don't do it. 

Speaking of being unpleasant to be around, Verse *24 It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.* 

Similar to **Proverbs 21:9** and 
**Proverbs 21:19:** the trouble with having a spiteful and argumentative wife. **Proverbs 19:13**...*and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping*.

These sayings are often either used as an illustration to say men have failed to properly rule their home, or worse, to say that husbands need to try and please their wives and keep them from being like this through "servant leadership," or wooing her. 

Similar to the cliche of Father's Day sermons lecturing men to "be better," and Mother's Day sermons on "How great moms are," the blame for strained relationships and a wife's behavior is placed almost entirely on the husband. 

Women have agency and are expected to walk in the Spirit and grow in grace and love. These examples in Proverbs are as much on women to gain understanding as the rebuke against men for their wrath. 

Wives, don't be as a continuous dropping to your husband. Don't be so unpleasant and brawling as to make your husband want to sleep in the wilderness or on the roof of the house, or in a corner of the attic. Again, **1 Peter 3:1-6**

*Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.*

We will see in **Proverbs 31** God's description of a good wife. But it begins here, in these earlier sayings, where God's word agrees with the man that it's awful to have to put up with an unpleasant and bickering wife.

Rounding chapter 25 out with some simple truths; *As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.* 

*A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.*

Giving reason for scoffers and mockers to blaspheme, or to laugh at the children of the Lord hurts the cause of Christ. The fall of a righteous man doesn't just affect him and his immediate circle, but can have wider ramifications, and offend many while the unrighteous gloat. 

*It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.*

Don't seek people's attention, to gain praise for whatever it is you've done or think you deserve credit for. Pride and arrogance are bad qualities, and you will get less glory than had you just did what you're supposed to and left it for others to recognize. Remember, even if other people don't see it and praise you, God sees it and will reward you for sincerely good efforts. 

*He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.*

Finally, control yourself. Don't have a negative spirit, bitter, self-serving, wrathful, but be cheerful and seek others' profit above your own. Don't be a froward man or a brawling woman. Don't bring shame on yourself or the cause of Christ.

*Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.*

Too much of a good thing is bad. Including your own company. Just as sweet honeycomb is a treat, when you over do it, imposing yourself on others can lead to them hating you. Know when you've worn out your welcome. 

Slander against a neighbor is as much violence as if you used a weapon of war against them. It is wicked, and they've a right to defend themselves as if it were an attack. Better to keep this in mind, be you a king among nations, or a suburban dad.

Having to trust unfaithful people in adversity like a broken tooth and a foot out of joint; a throbbing constant pain. 

Verse 20 describes someone trying to cheer a heavy heart with song as making it so much worse. Forcing happiness on those that are mourning is compared to taking away a garment in the cold. Grief is its own comfort. Sometimes people need to go through it. Love and prayers and fitly spoken words are needed. We get uncomfortable with other's broken heart and try too hard to "get them out of their funk." The Bible says it is *as vinegar upon nitre*, or baking soda. As the explosive chemical reaction overflows the container, so to it makes their grief all the more worse.
*Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.*

Continuing in **Proverbs 25**; the instruction for a holy king and kingdom, recorded under the command of King Hezekiah.

*Take away the wicked from before the king; and his throne shall be established in righteousness*.

**2 Kings 18:4**
*He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.*

Hezekiah made his priority upon taking the throne of Judah to do exactly what wise Solomon taught. Hezekiah sought the wisdom of God rather than the ways of his father, Ahaz. 

Verse 7 state not to put yourself in the presence of the king; wisdom echoed by Christ Jesus in His earthly ministry. 

**Luke 14:8-10**
*When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him; And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room. But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.*

Better to be a humble servant, given honor than to be a prideful person, promoting yourself. The end will be shame. God loves to expose the proud.

That potential shame should also dissuade you from entering hastily into contention with your neighbor. Weigh the outcome, especially if you lose. Seek to talk it out, first. 

*A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver. *Take care of what you say, rather than just reacting angrily. It may well be that you're wrong, and that humiliation will be what you are known for. 

Think about the times you have assumed ill intent or made accusations without knowing all of the matter, and the person who is the object of your ire turns out to be innocently ignorant of what he has done, or worse, you were not even wronged in the way you thought you were. How humiliating. Better to consider and approach with grace. Remember:

**Romans 12:18**
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Be a wise reprover; know what you are talking about and tell your cause to your brother or neighbor with care. You may find an obedient ear, willing to listen and work it out.

*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. God's glory is revealed from heaven both in the richness of His mercy upon believers, but His wrath upon those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Reprobation of **Romans 1**. The *blindness in part*, that has come over the circumcision of the flesh that salvation is come to the Gentiles circumcised of the heart. 

*As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.*

If you recall, Cyrus was predicted by name, revealed unto Isaiah by the Spirit, as well as the entire captivity. As we just saw in **Daniel 9**, he was studying Jeremiah and understood that the 70 years of captivity was near its end, because of the prophecy Jeremiah had made.

Praying for redemption from their captivity as promised by the Lord. He is fasting and praying intensely, for 3 weeks, in supplication to the Lord for mercy for the sins of the people. 

And so it begins

**Timeline of Days in Daniel 7 - 12**

**I. Daniel 8:13-14 – Vision of the Sanctuary Cleansing**

**Daniel 8:13-14**
*Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot? And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.
*
**II. Daniel 12:11-12 – Specific Time Periods**

**Daniel 12:11-12**
*And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. *

**III. Timeframe Breakdown

Total Period: 7 Years**

**Daniel 9:27**
*And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease…*
- The "week" equals 7 prophetic years, calculated as 2,520 days (7 x 360-day lunar year+a “leap month" of 30 days).

**First Half: 3.5 Years (Tribulation of the Saints, 1,260 Days)**

**Daniel 7:25**
*And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.*
 - This period of 1,260 days (3.5 x 360) represents the tribulation where the saints face persecution.

**Midpoint: Abomination of Desolation**

**Daniel 9:27**
*…and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate…*
 - Occurs at the 1,260-day mark, splitting the 7 years.

**Second Half: 3.5 Years (Great Tribulation, 1,260 Days + 30 Days)**

**Daniel 7:25**
*…a time and times and the dividing of time.*
 - Extends to 1,290 days: Daniel 12:11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.
 - Extra 30 Days: The 1,290 days include the 1,260 days of the second half plus an additional 30 days, likely an intercalary month in the Jewish lunar calendar to align the 360-day prophetic years with the solar calendar, ensuring proper timing of events.

**Additional 45 Days (Great Tribulation Concludes)**

**Daniel 12:12**
*Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.*
 - The 1,335 days extend 45 days beyond the 1,290 days (1,335 - 1,290 = 45).
 - Total 75 Days: The 30 days (1,290 - 1,260) plus 45 days (1,335 - 1,290) form a 75-day period of intensified great tribulation, overlapping the second half’s end, concluding key events.

**Wrath of God: 3.5 Years (Post-1,335 Days)**
The remaining time after the 1,335 days (approximately 1,260 days, calculated as 2,520 total days minus 1,260 tribulation days and 75 great tribulation days) aligns with the period of God’s wrath, following the conclusion of the great tribulation.

Continuing in **Luke 10**, we see a lawyer, a religious position, one who examines the law of Moses, come to Jesus and this man seeks to tempt Him. He asks a typically bad faith question, as the Pharisees and Sadducees often do to Jesus, looking to trip Him up in matters of the law. The premise of the question he poses to Jesus is wrong from the start; that he as a man can justify himself. He asks what shall I do to inherit eternal life? 

And Jesus, as He is wont to do in these situations, answers in a question, asking this expert in the letter of the law, what it says in scripture. 

 The lawyer answers *Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.*

Jesus replies *Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.*

The law certainly does say this, and as Jesus says elsewhere, the whole of it falls on these two commandments. And, if it were possible to keep the whole of the law, one would be righteous and obtain eternal life. But the Bible says this isn't possible, that all have fallen short. All have sinned. 

Sin is the transgression of the law, and so by the law comes knowledge of sin. The knowledge of sin brings understanding of our failings, and by this knowledge comes the need for salvation by faith, being unobtainable by man, driven by the needs and lusts of the flesh, and our own vain imaginings. This fallen state of man is there to remind us of our need for God to save us from our wicked hearts. For Christ to be the propitiation for our sin. To obtain eternal life not by our own doing, but by trusting in the promise of God, the blood of Christ, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, the circumcision of the heart. 

But the lawyer, we are told, *seeking to justify himself *asks, Who is my neighbor?

The implication is that these holy men, claiming to be experts in righteousness, believe they are righteous by their own ability. Instead of showing them their own failings that they may be ripe for repentance, their pride sees them lie to themselves that they do not sin, and keep the law. And so the lawyer believes He is about to be shown justified by this Jesus. Confirming he is righteous by his works. And so Jesus tells him the parable of the Good Samaritan. 

We all know it. It may be one of if not *the* most famous of Jesus teachings.

A man taken by robbers, left for dead on the side of the road. A priest of the temple crosses the street to avoid this poor soul needing help. A Levite, a servant of the temple, also a supposed man of God passes him by. But a man, not just any man, but a Samaritan, an enemy of the Jews, two people who despise each other as much for their shared lineage as their difference. No love lost between them. Enemies. 

And this Samaritan sees a man in need, and without thinking of self, without thinking of the enmity, he goes out of his way to help him. He takes time to care for someone near him, and in need.

The moral of the story being that that's what defines a neighbor. Someone in your immediate sphere of influence who needs help, and to whom you can give help.

The law says, in **Exodus 23:4** *If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again*. How much more your enemy himself?

And so, Jesus by His parable establishes just how high a bar the keeping of the law is. How much is expected of us who seek to justify ourselves, as this lawyer does. And with this, Jesus sends him on his way.

What is lost on the lawyer is what's lost on mankind from the very beginning; That by our works we cannot be justified. This is the lesson of Cain. It's the lesson Jesus seeks to show this lawyer. And Paul, writing in the epistles hammers this need for salvation by self-righteous works that we innately cling to as often being a stumbling block to faith rather than a schoolmaster to lead us to faith. 

All who are saved by faith understand that by our nature, man sins and in sin, we die. That the wages of sin is death. That there are none righteous, no not one.

Proclaiming that it is by faith alone. That, contrary to the vain wisdom of man, that it is the "foolishness of the cross" that we hold our hope in. 

But that's not entirely true.

Man may work his way to heaven. God gave us the means by which we are allowed to become self-righteous. If we only could.

God shows by promise and blessing His intention to offer salvation by faith to those who call upon His name, who diligently seek Him. And still man doesn't understand. Still they seek to justify themselves.

He asks Jesus what must he ***do*** to inherit eternal life. Calling Jesus "good master," Jesus tempts him asking why does he call Him good, for only God is good.  He who was God made flesh, repeatedly and habitually withdraws Himself to prayer. He prays to God at the start of His ministry. He prays during the highs and lows. **Leviticus 10:8-9**
*And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying, Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations:*

...and the numerous places in scripture that teach against it present a problem for those seeking to use this verse to justify it. 

But what then? First, we see the drink offering is to be poured out with the burnt offering, which is a continual fire. Alcoholic strong drink would feed the fire, where new wine would quench it. Ellicott's Commentary states:
(7) Shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured . . . --Better, pour out the drink offering of strong drink. The word shecar, which is here rendered "strong wine," denotes any kind of intoxicating drink, whether made from grapes, honey, or grain; but it is more frequently used to denote a drink which is not made from grapes, as, e.g., in Leviticus 10:9, where the command is given to Aaron and his sons not to drink "wine nor strong drink" (shecar) when they went into the tent of meeting. In the parallel passage in Exodus, the drink offering was to consist of "the fourth part of an hin of wine" (Numbers 29:40). (Comp. Numbers 15:5.) In Exodus 30:9 it is forbidden to pour any drink offering upon the altar of incense, from which passage it has been inferred that the drink offerings were poured upon the altar of burnt sacrifice.

The indication that strong wine is liquor from other sources than grapes, which has weak fermentation. 

Matthew Henry commentary says;
The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17.

I only note these to show that this passage is unique in what it commands, and the reason unclear other than to suppose it is a libation for God, and His will it be offered.

drive.title: Doeg
drive.text:
Psalm 52 is told to us as a Psalm written when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech.

The situation is described in 1 Samuel 21, David has fled Saul, who is determined to kill him. Consumed with pride and evil spirits, the king seeks the life of a man considered a hero among Israel.

David seeks food and weapons at the Tabernacle in Nob, from the unsuspecting priest, Ahimelech. Ahimelech unwittingly provides David with the shew bread, and Goliath’s sword as David claims he is on a secret mission for the King.

**1 Samuel 21:2**
*And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know any thing of the business whereabout I send thee, and what I have commanded thee: and I have appointed my servants to such and such a place.*

(An act that Jesus uses to justify His Apostles plucking corn to eat on the Sabbath. Matthew 12:3-4 Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him; How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?)

But the priest isn’t the only person there to see David.

**1 Samuel 21:7**
*Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.*

Now, Doeg is not a man of war. He is a herdsman. He oversees the other shepherds and wranglers for the King. But he took the opportunity of seeing David there in Nob, on the run, to curry favor with Saul.

The story continues, showing David’s flight, ending up in Judah at the advice of the prophet Gad, bringing his parents to the King of Moab for protection, and gathering with him loyal men as he went.

**1 Samuel 22:2**
*And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.*

(This is a lovely picture of Jesus and salvation, the distressed and debtors gathering unto him.)

Saul hears tell of these activities;

**1 Samuel 22:6–7**
*When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul abode in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;) Then Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, ye Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;*

As Saul assembles his armies, Doeg enters the picture;

**1 Samuel 22:9–10**
*Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. And he enquired of the LORD for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.*

We should note that much time has passed since David’s flight to Nob, and Saul has an idea of where David and his men have hidden, in the forest of Hareth, in Judah.

But Doeg brings his knowledge to the King as he is already readying for war. It feels even more opportunistic and craven in light of that passage of time and the context. Doeg’s word causes Saul to summon the priest and his kin;

**1 Samuel 22:11–13**
*Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king. And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord. And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?*

The hapless Ahimelech then pleads ignorance and asks that Saul understand that he had no way of knowing David fled the King.

**1 Samuel 22:15–16**
*Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.*
*And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.*

Saul refuses clemency. In his murderous rage he orders the death of the priest and entire lineage.

**1 Samuel 22:17**
*And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD: because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.*

Even Saul’s loyal men hesitate and refuse the order of their King, out of fear of the Lord and harming His anointed priests. In the state the King was in, in the context of his twisted, murderous vengeance, the footmen feared God more.

But not Doeg the Edomite.

**1 Samuel 22:18–19**
*And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod. And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.*

Doeg the shepherd, Doeg the herdsman, who brought out of date intelligence to Saul’s attention, jeopardizing the priest, that led to this situation, took full advantage of the license given him by Saul, and wickedly carried out the command. First slaying 85 priests, and then murdering every man, woman, and child, beast and all, found in the Levite city of Nob.

One of the sons of Ahimelech escapes to see David, telling him of the wicked act done at the hands of Doeg;

**1 Samuel 22:20–23**
*And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David. And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests. And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house. Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.*

David’s guilt at not taking care of Doeg when he had the opportunity, and the resulting deaths, has him offer Abiathar refuge with him and his troop of men.

David will have Abiathar act in his office, with the ephod, to consult with the Lord several times. Asking Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? And later, enquiring of the Lord, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? Seeking the wisdom of God to direct his paths in times of uncertainty.

David, in exile, is given the oracles of God through the Levite and ephod, as a King would. Saul, in his rage had cut himself off from this avenue of prophecy. As the sole survivor of the high priestly line of Eli, Abiathar brings the official religious authority of Israel to David’s camp, signaling that God has abandoned Saul.

By using the Urim and Thummim in the ephod, Abiathar provides divine reconnaissance that saves David from Saul’s traps and ensures the defeat of the Amalekites. Abiathar serves as David’s high priest throughout his exile and reign, eventually helping bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem.

During Absalom’s rebellion, Abiathar remains behind in Jerusalem to act as a secret agent, feeding David crucial intelligence through his son Jonathan to help win back the throne.

The evil of Saul and the bloodthirst of Doeg, became good for David, who loved God and was called according to His purpose.

But Doeg became a byword.

Psalm 52 mockingly called Doeg a "mighty man," for slaying men of God, dressed only in linen, and helpless women and children, even babies. Doeg did what was unthinkable to the actual mighty men of Saul, after causing the entire situation by his obsequious talebearing. Immortalized in his wickedness by the psalmist, David.

**Psalm 52:1–3**
*Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually. Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.*

We can imagine Doeg’s fate, the Bible doesn’t speak specifically of what became of him afterwards, but Psalm 52 gives us some idea of his ultimate fate before God.

**Psalm 52:5–7**
*God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah. The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.*

But by his evil, good came. David trusted in the mercy of the Lord, and was strengthened by Doeg’s actions, and was able to sing of the praises of the Lord because of it.

drive.text:
Psalm 53 opens with one of the clearest and concise views of the nature of the atheist.

While it is, in context, about the man who denies God to do evil, lacking fear in Him who he cannot see, and so, unchecked and without fear proceeds to work iniquity, that is ultimately the driving force behind so-called "intellectual atheism" as well. The danger of this delusion leading to reprobation is very real.

The brute beast of man, ignoring the evidence of God; His wrath revealed from Heaven against the wicked, His mercy upon the faithful, the very creation that proclaims His power and glory, will engage in all manner of evil, justified within his desperately wicked heart, until God gives him up to his vile affections. Searing his conscience, giving him over to a reprobate mind, and he is filled with all unrighteousness.

Taken to the logical end, the fool who began by denying the existence of God, will ultimately become rejected utterly if they continue in their error.

**Romans 1:19–24**
*Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*

But the general meaning here in Psalm 53 can apply to all men who don’t know or understand the truth. Well before their being made twice-dead. And it is a warning that can still prick at the heart of the lost, while there is yet time.

It is Paul’s paraphrase of this Psalm that we use when we give the gospel to people;

**Romans 3:10–12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

This truth, that we are all sinners, is often sufficient to bring a person to at least hear the salvation plan. But first they have to acknowledge that God is.

Usually, if a person admits to the reality of God and does not try to excuse away His existence, getting them to admit they are a sinner is easy. They won’t disagree with the scripture when it says Every one of them is gone back: they are altogether become filthy; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

But the fool who denies God will balk at that characterization. The atheist will claim that they do not need fear of God to "do good." That they keep the commandment to love their neighbors, and reject that they are sinners.

Of course this is delusional. But even on the surface level, they are acknowledging a truth of the God who they reject existing, a morality that comes explicitly from Him, from the law written in our hearts, by the rebuke of the Spirit those who aren’t reprobate, feel.

**Romans 2:14–15**
*For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)*

They are fish who deny they are wet.

And their judgment against others, accusing and excusing the sins of other men, betrays their own heart that denies the truth, by accepting God’s work in them, and His judgement.

**Romans 2:1–3**
*Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things. But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things. And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?*

This internal conflict between their wicked hearts and the conscience of the Spirit will often bring the fool, the "intellectual atheist," out of it. The cognitive dissonance will trigger repentance for many. There are great Christians who were once seduced by the foolishness of their heart into denying His truth. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, but in their foolishness, God’s word preached unto them triggers a change of heart, and an acceptance of the reality of God, before it is "too late, reprobate."

But for many, they seek to deny the conflict in their hearts, and they seek to cauterize their conscience, and not wishing to retain God in their knowledge, they prefer to believe a lie.

*Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread: they have not called upon God. There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.*

The reprobate lives in constant fear. They know the truth somewhere in themselves, but have built up strong walls against it, hardening their hearts and ultimately God hardens it completely. They live in constant fear, trapped in a fight or flight mode. And it leads them to do evermore wicked things, as God scatters their bones.

**Romans 1:29–32**
*Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

God hath despised them.

We may lament, as David does here, wondering Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? Do they not understand how God is already judging them? We often cannot comprehend the unsaved person’s refusal to see the truth, let alone one given up and given over to a reprobate mind. Don’t they see the sudden destruction they are headed for?

But our inability to think like they do shouldn’t keep us from understanding they exist. We are to be wise as serpents, Jesus said. And so, like righteous Lot, we are vexed by their filthy conversation.

*Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.*

The prayer of David that the deliverer come, the day of the Lord, the judgment of God’s wrath upon a wicked world, is the same prayer we have today for the coming again of Christ. Thy Kingdom come. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

He will deal with the tares and the goats and all the fools who have denied God in their hearts. Come quickly, Lord Jesus. Amen

It should be noted that Psalm 53 directly mirrors Psalm 14, the major difference is the Lord vs God in its language, while the content is close to identical.

We can draw application from this, that the LORD is God and vice versa. The foolish idea some propose that there are different Gods in the Old Testament, can be debunked strictly from this minor distinction within the same language and theme.

But we can also draw out the importance of understanding the heart and mind of those that not only reject God’s judgment against their wicked deeds, but their delusional heart that denies He even exists, in order to give them excuse for their evil.

Psalm 54 is another prayerful song that was penned by David during his flight from Saul.

**1 Samuel 23:14-15**
*And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand. And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.*

Shortly after making his refuge in the woods of Ziph, Saul's son Jonathan comes to David and assures his beloved friend that his father will not find him.

**1 Samuel 23:16-18**
*And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God. And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth. And they two made a covenant before the LORD: and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.*

Credited as a Psalm of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us? We can sense the urgency of David's prayer to God, with the plaintive Save me, and Hear my prayer.

**1 Samuel 23:19-21**
*Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon? Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand. And Saul said, Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me.*

There are times in our life when the relative safety we have is suddenly threatened. When even strangers rise up against us, and we have unexpected enemies that we weren't even aware of...when in desperation we should turn to God.

Behold, God is my helper. This simple truth is reassuring in our time of trouble.

And blessing on those who have our backs, who give us comfort and support, should be in our prayers as well. David says, the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.

In the Psalm, we see David praising those that help him, (mirroring King Saul's blessing upon the Ziphites for revealing David's hiding spot. The irony here is interesting. Especially given the context). The Ziphites and Saul pursue David, but he makes his escape to Maon.

This sudden threat rising against the future King, God's anointed, troubles him enough to bring him to call for God's mercy, to deliver him with His strength, to reward his enemies for the evil they sought to do to him. To bless those that stand with him.

What a model for believers to have, so when our fear rises, we have the assurance of this Psalm to guide us in prayer, along with the results; God delivers us from all trouble, He takes vengeance on our enemies for us. All that we may give praise to His holy name. Amen
